fælles.explanation: "Fælles" means "shared". To say two people both know the same person, it means "mutual": "Vi har en fælles bekendt" (We have a mutual acquaintance).

fælleskøn.explanation: "Et fælleskøn" means "a common gender". It is built from "fælles" (shared) and "køn" (gender). A word of common gender takes "en" before it: "en stol" (a chair).

fængslende.explanation: "Fængslende" means "captivating". It comes from the verb "at fængsle" (to imprison). To praise a film, say: "Filmen var fængslende" (The film was captivating).

færdig.explanation: "Færdig" means "finished". To say you are ready to start, use "klar" (ready) instead: "Er du klar?" (Are you ready?).

færdig med.explanation: "Færdig med" means "finished with". To say what you finished, put it after "med": "Jeg er færdig med lektierne" (I am finished with the homework). To say you finished doing something, add "at" before the verb: "Jeg er færdig med at spise" (I am finished eating).

færdiglavet.explanation: "Færdiglavet" means "ready-made". It is built from "færdig" (ready) and "lavet" (made).

færre.explanation: "Færre" means "fewer". To say fewer of things you can count, use "færre": "færre biler" (fewer cars). With something you cannot count, such as noise, use "mindre" (less): "mindre støj" (less noise).

færøerne.explanation: "Færøerne" means "the Faroe Islands". They belong to the Kingdom of Denmark but govern themselves in many matters. To say you are there, use "på" (on): "Vi bor på Færøerne" (We live on the Faroe Islands).

færøsk.explanation: "Færøsk" means "Faroese", as in from the Faroe Islands. It also means the language. Unlike English, Danish spells it without a big first letter, even for the language: "Hun taler færøsk" (She speaks Faroese).

føj.explanation: "Føj" means "yuck". To react when you see something disgusting, say: "Føj, hvor er det klamt!" (Yuck, how gross that is!).

følelsesmæssigt.explanation: "Følelsesmæssigt" means "emotionally". It is built from "en følelse" (a feeling) and the ending "-mæssigt", which is also in "tidsmæssigt" (time-wise).

følgende.explanation: "Følgende" means "following". The form does not change after "den", "det" or "de": "den følgende dag" (the following day), "de følgende dage" (the following days). To start a list, say: "Medbring følgende: pas og billet" (Bring the following: passport and ticket).

følsom.explanation: "Følsom" means "sensitive". To talk about skin or things that react easily, say: "følsom hud" (sensitive skin). To say what someone reacts to, add "over for" (to): "følsom over for kritik" (sensitive to criticism).

før.explanation: "Før" means "before". To say who comes earlier, say: "Jeg kommer før dig" (I come before you). To say in front of a place, use "foran" (in front of) instead: "Vi står foran huset" (We stand in front of the house).

førdatid.explanation: "En førdatid" means "a past perfect". To say something happened before another past event, build it with "havde" (had): "Hun havde spist, før jeg kom" (She had eaten before I came). With verbs of movement, use "var" (was): "Hun var gået, da jeg kom" (She had left when I came).

førende.explanation: "Førende" means "leading". It comes from the verb "at føre" (to lead). To say a company is a top one in its field, say: "Det er et førende firma inden for solenergi" (It is a leading firm in solar energy).

førnutid.explanation: "En førnutid" means "a present perfect". To say what has happened up to now, build it with "har" (have): "Jeg har købt brød" (I have bought bread). With verbs of movement, use "er" (am, is): "Han er rejst" (He has left).

først.explanation: "Først" means "first". To say something comes before the rest, say: "Du går først" (You go first). To say something does not happen until a time, it means "not until": "Jeg kommer først i morgen" (I am not coming until tomorrow). To say the first one in a list, use "første" (first) instead: "den første dag" (the first day).

først og fremmest.explanation: "Først og fremmest" means "first and foremost". To name your main point before the smaller ones, say: "Først og fremmest tak for hjælpen" (First and foremost, thank you for the help).

første.explanation: "Første" means "first". In dates, use it for the day number: "den første maj" (the first of May), written "1. maj". To say what happens first, use "først" (first) instead: "Først spiser vi" (First we eat).

førstehjælp.explanation: "Førstehjælp" means "first aid". It is built from "første" (first) and "hjælp" (help). To name the box that holds the supplies, say: "en førstehjælpskasse" (a first aid box).

at gabe.explanation: "At gabe" means "to yawn". It also describes a big opening: "Hullet gaber" (The hole gapes).

at gange.explanation: "At gange" means "to multiply". To say you multiply numbers, say: "Jeg ganger to med tre" (I multiply two by three). It comes from "gange" (times): "Tre gange to er seks" (Three times two is six).

at garantere.explanation: "At garantere" means "to guarantee". To say you guarantee something, say: "Jeg garanterer, at den virker" (I guarantee that it works). To say you promise to do something, use "at love" (to promise): "Jeg lover at komme" (I promise to come).

at gemme.explanation: "At gemme" means "to save", as in saving a file: "Husk at gemme filen" (Remember to save the file). To put something where nobody finds it, it means "to hide": "Hun gemte nøglen" (She hid the key).
